title: What is React?
description: Understand what React is, its history, why it became popular, and how it compares to other frameworks.

data.text: **React** is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. It was created by Jordan Walke, a software engineer at Meta (then Facebook), and was first deployed on Facebook's newsfeed in 2011. React was open-sourced in 2013 and has since become the most widely adopted frontend library in the world.

Before React, developers built UIs by manually manipulating the DOM. Every time data changed, you found the right element and updated it. As apps grew, this became error-prone and slow. React introduced the **Virtual DOM** — a lightweight copy of the real DOM — so it could calculate the cheapest set of changes and apply them in one batch.
React is often compared to Angular and Vue. While all three build UIs, they take different approaches to structure, performance, and learning curve.
React and Vue are the closest in philosophy: both use a component model, virtual DOM, and reactive data. The main differences are in template syntax and ecosystem.

cards.title: React

pros: Flexible architecture — pick your own router and state library
JSX gives you the full power of JavaScript in templates
cons: More decisions to make (router, state, styling)

cards.title: Vue

pros: Gentler learning curve with HTML-based templates
Official router and state management included
cons: Fewer enterprise positions compared to React

terms.definition: A reusable, self-contained piece of UI built with JavaScript and JSX.
A syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like code inside JavaScript.
Data that changes over time inside a component, triggering re-renders.
Read-only inputs passed from parent to child components.
A lightweight JavaScript representation of the real DOM used for efficient updates.

data.text: React encourages **declarative** code: you describe what the UI should look like for a given state, and React figures out how to update the DOM. This is different from **imperative** DOM manipulation where you manually change elements step by step.

data.text: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces.
React apps are trees of components. Each component manages its own state and renders JSX. You compose small components into larger ones, creating a modular and maintainable codebase.

data.title: Reasons for Adoption
items: **Performance**: Virtual DOM and efficient reconciliation make updates fast.
**Reusability**: Components can be shared across projects and teams.
**Ecosystem**: Rich set of libraries for routing, state, forms, and testing.
**Community**: Massive community support, tutorials, and job opportunities.
**Flexibility**: Use React for web, mobile (React Native), and desktop.

data.alt: React logo and a diagram showing component composition
data.caption: React enables building complex UIs from small, reusable components.

data.title: Exercise: Identify React Concepts
data.description: Review a simple HTML page and identify parts that could become React components.
steps: Open any static website (e.g., a blog or product page).
List the major UI sections you see (header, sidebar, footer, etc.).
Sketch how you would break them into React components.
Identify which parts would need state and which would only use props.
data.expectedOutcome: A mental model of how to translate a static page into a React component tree.

items.question: Is React a framework or a library?
items.answer: React is a library. It handles the view layer. You choose additional libraries for routing (React Router), state (Redux, Zustand), and side effects.

items.question: Do I need to know JavaScript deeply before React?
items.answer: Yes. React is JavaScript. Comfort with ES6+ features like arrow functions, destructuring, modules, and promises will make React much easier.

items.question: What is the latest React version?
items.answer: React 19 is the latest major release at the time of this writing, introducing the React Compiler, Actions, the use() hook, and improved Server Components.

items.question: Can I use React without JSX?
items.answer: Yes, using React.createElement, but JSX is strongly recommended because it is more readable and is the standard in the React ecosystem.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: React is a JavaScript library for building component-based user interfaces.
It uses a Virtual DOM for efficient updates and reconciliation.
React is declarative: you describe the UI, and React updates the DOM.
It has the largest frontend ecosystem and a vibrant job market.
React 19 brings the compiler, Actions, use(), and improved Server Components.
data.takeaway: You now understand what React is and why it became the world's most popular frontend library. Next, we'll set up your development environment.
